title: Finite-basis coordinates for constant scalar extension
statement:
Finite-free constant scalar extension, after forgetting to abelian presheaves, is naturally a finite power of the underlying-presheaf functor. No countability assumption and no product preservation occurs.

theorem constantFiniteFree_underlyingPowerIso
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J CommRingCat.{max uC vC r}]
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max uC vC r} RingCat.{max uC vC r})]
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    (A B : CommRingCat.{max uC vC r}) [Algebra A B] [Module.Free A B]
    [Module.Finite A B]
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max uC vC r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj
          ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat).obj A)) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{max uC vC r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj
          ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat).obj B)))
    (hobj : ∀ M, F.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses
      ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat).map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B))) M)
    (hmap : ∀ M N (f : M ⟶ N), HEq (F.map f)
      (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHomOfUniverses
        ((constantSheaf J CommRingCat).map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B))) M f)) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty
      (F ⋙ SheafOfModules.forget _ ⋙ PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _ ≅
        (SheafOfModules.forget _ ⋙ PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _) ⋙
          Functor.const (Discrete (Fin n)) ⋙ lim)

proof.text: Use lem-pur-constant-finite-free-section-basis for compatible section bases. TensorProduct.piScalarRight and the basis coordinate linear equivalence identify each sectionwise tensor with a finite power. The coordinate maps commute with restriction by tensor induction and the basis restriction formula. Their inverses are verified by the basis identities; functor-category evaluation preserves products, so these give a presheaf isomorphism. Tensor induction also proves naturality in module maps. Apply additive sheafification and its natural unit isomorphism on the finite power of a module sheaf, which is a sheaf because sheaves are closed under products. Finally conjugate by the given object equalities using the heterogeneous map equalities, and use Pi.isoLimit to identify the finite product with the displayed limit. All assembly is proved in Lean.
